Ready for the maintainer to merge. No blocking findings. This is the safety-tier Opus review that the author asked for on this head.

## Earlier review

The earlier review on `215d44a52` was clean and had no findings. The head did not change. The author put the PR back to draft for an Opus review of the safety tier. I did a full review of the same head. I found no new blocker, so the verdict stays clean.

## Safety tier

The PR does not change a generator, a gouge check or a collision check. It changes the parameter that the edit stores: Helix becomes Arc in one case. This changes the generated entry motion of that operation, so I reviewed it at the safety tier.

What I checked:

- The Arc entry of a start-side pass is the air entry of #3746 (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/air_entry.rs`). It plunges outside the stock box and proves the lead against the part and the rings. Where no lead fits, it uses a named stand-in entry or a named refusal. It does not plunge silently.
- Where no air room applies, the Arc arm in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/descent.rs` falls back by name, the same as for a user who selects Arc today. The PR adds no new motion path. It only selects an entry that a user can already select.
- The law runs in `EditOperationParams::edit` before `infeed_plan_gate`, `named_refusal` and `is_sane`. Thus the Arc value goes through all the validation gates.
- The command stores `prev` and `next` as a whole. One undo restores Auto and Helix together. The integration pin proves this.
- The GUI page: after each edit, `sync_ops_ui` reads the operation again from the world (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:2716`, keyed on `doc_version`). The page draft thus shows Arc after the edit. A later Apply or Generate does not send the old Helix back.
- No recorded program changed. The example catalog suites pass.

- Upstream main: `f2aa981b51a3453428fb294c6c71c575a0178ef6`.
- Trial merge: no conflicts. HEAD^1 is the PR head.
- All commands ran locally on macOS. No GitHub runner ran.
- I checked the laws against the AGENTS.md of this upstream main.

## Mutations

I selected two mutations that are different from the two in the PR body and the earlier review:

1. Remove the call `params.with_start_side_entry(&prev.params)` in `edit.rs`. RED: both integration pins fail. `a_start_side_edit_of_a_seeded_offset_takes_arc_and_undo_restores_helix` fails at line 61 (`left: (Inside, Helix)`, `right: (Inside, Arc)`). `mcp_start_side_edit_takes_arc_and_a_later_helix_choice_stays` fails at line 84. Restored: GREEN.
2. Remove the guard `*entry == Entry3D::Helix` (the entry after the edit). RED: `a_user_choice_of_entry_stays` fails at line 71 (`left: Some(Arc)`, `right: Some(Plunge)`). Restored: GREEN.

After the restores, the worktree has no changes and the four pins pass.

## Goldens moved

None. No `*.nc`, `*.cl`, `examples/catalog/**` or `tests/golden/` file changed. The body says "None", and this agrees with the file list.

## Law check

- Prime Directive: `expect` and `panic!` occur only in tests. The new law has no numeric code.
- Everything Is a Command: the law is in the command. Every door gets it, and undo is one step.
- Code shape: the new module has a provenance line and 92 lines. `edit.rs` has 380 lines.
- Placement: the new test file is a submodule of the existing `offset_pass_start` suite. It imports `camcraft_app` commands and MCP. It adds no test binary.
- No new crate dependency. No process file. No UI source change, so no screenshots are necessary.
- The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends with `Fixes #3843`. The commit subject is conventional. The decision is in `docs/decisions/3843-start-side-arc.md`.
- Heavy lanes: not run. They are not a merge condition. The author ran the ignored `offset_pass_start` tests.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Optional, non-blocking

- One MCP call that sets `pass_start` to Inside or Outside and also sets `entry` to `helix` on a seeded operation gets Arc. The law cannot see that the caller wrote Helix again. The reply shows `"entry":"arc"`, and a second edit keeps Helix. The decision file accepts this. A short note in the MCP tool text can tell agents about it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 215d44a52723cecbad5aba19eb3d82dcb5b5b55d -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge. No P1-class finding. Two follow-ups for the merging session to file (see below).

## Why this review is clean

I started this full safety-tier review before the Opus review of 09:04Z on the same head was posted. That review is clean. By the re-review rule, a new finding on the same head sets `needs-rework` only if it is P1-class. My two findings are not P1-class: Helix and Arc are both valid, proved entries, and each result is visible in the MCP answer. Thus I list them as follow-ups. Without the earlier clean review, I would request the changes before merge, because each finding is a gap in the "Done means" of #3843.

## Scope

The PR changes the stored entry of a 2D Offset. The entry selects the descent motion, so it can change posted G-code. Thus this is a safety-tier review. The PR adds no motion code. The Arc entry is an existing, user-selectable entry with its own chord proof and named substitutes (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/descent.rs:267-282`). I found no gouge risk in the change.

## What looks good

- The law is in the command, before validation. One undo restores Auto and Helix together. Redo takes the stored `next`.
- The law has no `unwrap`, no panic and no numeric work.
- The new tests join the existing `offset_pass_start` directory suite. No new test binary.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/3843-start-side-arc.md` is present. The provenance lines are present. Each new file is under 400 lines.
- The commit subject is conventional. The body ends with `Fixes #3843`. The PR body has a `Changelog:` line.
- No `*.nc`, `*.cl`, `examples/catalog/**` or `tests/golden/` file changed. "Goldens moved: None" agrees with the diff.
- No `crates/ui` change, so no screenshots are necessary.

## Results (locally, trial merge with upstream/main)

- PR head `215d44a52723cecbad5aba19eb3d82dcb5b5b55d`, upstream/main `f2aa981b51a3453428fb294c6c71c575a0178ef6`. The merge had no conflicts.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 34 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `app suites: lib`, `offset_pass_start`, `mcp` and `mcp_order`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Heavy lanes: not run. This is a P3 PR ("Heavy lanes at review").

Extra suites run:
- `app suites: example_catalog`: ok.
- `app suites: example_catalog_adaptive`: ok.
- `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work`: ok.
- No `testdata/` change and no importer change, so no other extra suites apply.

## Mutations (each restored after the run)

1. Remove the `with_start_side_entry` call in `crates/app/src/commands/operation/edit.rs:114`. Result: red. The two integration pins fail (`left: (Inside, Helix)`, `right: (Inside, Arc)`).
2. Remove the `*entry == Entry3D::Helix` guard in `crates/app/src/operation/types/start_side_entry.rs:26`. Result: red. `a_user_choice_of_entry_stays` fails at line 71.

## Follow-ups (file after merge)

The two findings have one class. The law reads only the values before and after an edit. It does not see what the request named. One rule can close the class: the door tells the law if the request named an entry, and the create door applies the same law against the seed.

1. **P3 - the create door does not get the law.** `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:308-311`: `add_operation` patches the seed and calls `CreateOperation` directly. A probe that I ran (not committed):
   `add_operation {"kind":"2D Offset", "params":{"pass_start":"outside"}}` gives `pass_start: outside`, `entry: helix`.
   This is the bug of #3843 at a different door. The issue says: "A 2D Offset with "Pass starts at" Inside or Outside uses Arc unless the user selects another type".

2. **P3 - an explicit Helix in the same request is replaced with Arc.** `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:323-324`: `edit_operation` merges the patch onto the current params, so the law cannot see a named entry. A probe that I ran (not committed), on a new 2D Offset:
   `edit_operation {"params":{"pass_start":"inside","entry":"helix"}}` gives `pass_start: inside`, `entry: arc`.
   The user selected Helix and got a different entry. The decision file does not list this case. A GUI page that sends the start side and the entry in one edit has the same problem. I probed the MCP door only.

Each follow-up needs an MCP pin in `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start/start_side_entry.rs`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
